# Contamination estimate

The bundled NIPAT implementation integrates NEWPAT commit
`9c2a8be60afcb944153710da6a61cd0559e2b4cf` and retains bounded parallel sample and
row processing with ordered statistical reductions. Run it through the NIPAT
runtime, which supplies the configuration and execution helpers.

Inspect all thresholds and model constants with `nipat settings contamination`.
The homozygous thresholds, `other_fraction_max` and `include_zero` can be changed
with `--set contamination.PARAMETER=VALUE` or a `--scientific-config` JSON file;
every run records the effective values. Native `--include_zero`/`--exclude_zero`
options override the configured zero policy when explicitly supplied.
Supplying both native zero-policy flags is rejected. The output file
`scientific-settings.json` records the final parameters and model constants.

This module estimates the proportion of unexpected-allele reads at sites classified as homozygous, using count tables generated by [SNPcall](../SNPcall) or [DNPcall](https://github.com/fravasini/DNPcall).

## Requirements

- R ≥ 4.4.2
- R package: `dplyr` ≥ 1.1.4
- `tools`, included with R

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lpistacchia/NEWPAT.git
cd NEWPAT/contamination
```

## Inputs

The script requires:

- A SNP or DNP marker list.
- A single calling output file or a directory containing calling outputs.

Marker lists must be tab-separated. Lists with or without a header are accepted.

| Type | Marker-list columns |
|---|---|
| SNP | `chr`, `pos`, `REF`, `ALT` |
| DNP | `chr`, `pos1`, `pos2`, `REF`, `ALT` |

Lists containing only the coordinate columns are also accepted.

Calling outputs must contain the corresponding coordinates and `N_REF`, `N_ALT`, and `N_Other`. For details on these tables, see the SNPcall and DNPcall documentation.

Use a directory containing only calling output tables. Subdirectories are searched recursively. Save results outside the input directory.

## Usage

Arguments follow this order:

```text
marker_list  input_path  output_directory
```

### DNP example

```bash
Rscript detect_contamination.R \
  examples/inputs/DNP/markers.txt \
  examples/inputs/DNP/calling_outputs \
  results_DNP
```

### SNP example

```bash
Rscript detect_contamination.R \
  examples/inputs/SNP/markers.txt \
  examples/inputs/SNP/calling_outputs \
  results_SNP
```

To analyse one sample, replace the input directory with its file path:

```bash
Rscript detect_contamination.R \
  examples/inputs/DNP/markers.txt \
  examples/inputs/DNP/calling_outputs/SampleA.txt \
  results_SampleA
```

The marker type is detected automatically. The panel and calling outputs must use the same format.

## Sites with no unexpected reads

By default, sites with `N_unexpected = 0` are included in the calculation.

To exclude them, add `--exclude_zero`:

```bash
Rscript detect_contamination.R \
  examples/inputs/DNP/markers.txt \
  examples/inputs/DNP/calling_outputs \
  results_DNP_nozero \
  --exclude_zero
```

The same option applies to SNP inputs. `--include_zero` can be supplied explicitly, but is already the default.

This choice affects the retained sites, their number, the mean and the standard deviation.

## Calculation

The script retains panel sites classified as homozygous:

- REF homozygote: `N_REF / (N_REF + N_ALT) ≥ 0.90`.
- ALT homozygote: `N_REF / (N_REF + N_ALT) ≤ 0.10`.

Sites without REF or ALT reads are excluded. 

```text
N_Other / (N_REF + N_ALT + N_Other) ≤ 0.10
```

At each retained site, `N_unexpected` is the number of ALT reads in a REF homozygote, or REF reads in an ALT homozygote.

The site-level estimate is:

```text
contamination = N_unexpected / (N_REF + N_ALT)
```

The sample estimate is the arithmetic mean across retained sites. Values are proportions: multiply by 100 to obtain percentages.

Unexpected reads may also reflect sequencing errors or other artifacts. 

## Outputs

All tables are tab-separated `.txt` files.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `contamination_<sample>.txt` | Retained sites, original count columns and calculated ratios |
| `contamination_summary.txt` | One summary row per sample |

The summary contains:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `individuo` | Sample name, taken from the input filename |
| `informative_sites` | Number of retained sites |
| `mean_contamination` | Mean site-level estimate |
| `sd_contamination` | Standard deviation across retained sites |

If no sites remain, the mean and standard deviation are `NA`. With one retained site, only the standard deviation is `NA`.

Example outputs for SNPs and DNPs, with zeros included and excluded, are available in `examples/outputs/`.
